description: Lanthanum is a soft, ductile, silvery-white metal with symbol La and atomic number 57. It is the first element and prototype of the lanthanide series, a group of 15 similar elements in the periodic table, and is traditionally counted among the rare-earth elements. Its usual oxidation state is +3, although some compounds with an oxidation state of +2 are known.
uses: Lanthanum compounds have numerous applications including catalysts, additives in glass, carbon arc lamps for studio lights and projectors, ignition elements in lighters and torches, electron cathodes, scintillators, and gas tungsten arc welding electrodes. Lanthanum carbonate is used as a phosphate binder to treat high levels of phosphate in the blood accompanied by kidney failure.
characteristics: Lanthanum is a soft metal that tarnishes slowly when exposed to air and can readily burn to form lanthanum(III) oxide. It has a relatively high electrical resistivity of 615 nΩm at room temperature, a hexagonal crystal structure at room temperature, and a melting point of 920 °C. Among the lanthanides, lanthanum is exceptional in having no 4f electrons as a single gas-phase atom and is the least volatile of the lanthanides.
